deliverables.text: A monthly GPU-hour demand sequence: recursive rule and closed form, months 1-24, low/mid/high growth scenarios.
Two 24-month total-cost series (Long Lock, Open Tap), written as explicit sums, term by term.
Convergence/divergence classification of the Open Tap's monthly-cost series extended past 24 months, with the common ratio identified.
Total cost per GPU-hour delivered, both options, all three growth scenarios (six results in one table).
The crossover growth rate at which both series' 24-month totals produce the same cost per GPU-hour delivered.
A recommendation to the board, defended with D4 and D5, including what would have to be true for the recommendation to be wrong.

appendices.title: Kestrel's Board Directive and Decision Constraints
The Long Lock — 3-Year Fixed-Rate GPU Cluster Lease
The Open Tap — On-Demand GPU Capacity

balance.argument_a: The Long Lock's $2.97/GPU-hr fixed rate is 56.8% below the Open Tap's $6.88/GPU-hr on-demand rate, and at 100% utilization of the 512-GPU commitment that gap alone would decide it. Even at the High scenario (2.1%/month, 29%/year), the Long Lock's cost-per-GPU-hour-delivered ($7.21) is only 4.6% above the Open Tap's $6.88 — not a rout, a near-tie — and the exact tie point (D5's crossover) is ≈2.48%/month, ≈34.2%/year, just 5.2 annualized points above the High scenario's own 29%. Kestrel does not need to hit some exotic growth rate to make the Long Lock win: DigitalOcean, the same company Appendix D's own range is sourced from, is already guiding to over 50% revenue growth for 2027 and reporting its booked-but-unrealized pipeline (RPO) up more than 10x year over year — both comfortably past the 34.2% crossover. If Kestrel's real trajectory tracks that forward signal rather than its trailing 12 months, the Long Lock wins.
balance.argument_b: Run the case's own D4 table and the Open Tap wins all three scenarios: Low $6.88 vs. Long Lock's $8.13/GPU-hr (margin 15.4%), Mid $6.88 vs. $7.57 (margin 9.1%), High $6.88 vs. $7.21 (margin 4.6%). The Long Lock's $26,641,608 24-month bill is fixed regardless of usage — Appendix B says so outright — and at these DigitalOcean-sourced, mid-size-company growth rates (1.1%-2.1%/month, nowhere near a hyperscaler's pace), total demand over 24 months tops out around 3.3-3.7 million GPU-hours, spreading that fixed bill thin enough that the Open Tap's flat $6.88/GPU-hr beats it at every scenario the case actually models, without exception. The crossover the Long Lock camp leans on (34.2%/year) is not in Appendix D's range — it is a forward bet on a *different* number (DigitalOcean's own guidance for a future year) standing in for a number Kestrel does not have.
balance.margin_basis: Sum each option's 24-month cost series (D2), divide by total GPU-hours delivered over the same window, for each of the low/mid/high growth scenarios (D4). GPU-hours delivered = the D1 demand sequence itself (120,000 x (1+r)^t, t=0..23) for both options -- Appendix B states the Long Lock's *cost* is fixed regardless of usage, but no appendix states a hard physical delivery ceiling, so 'delivered' is read as 'demanded and served,' consistent with how both options are described. Long Lock's 24-month total cost is constant ($2.97/GPU-hr x 512 GPUs x 730 hr/month x 24 = $26,641,608) regardless of scenario, since Appendix B's fixed rate never changes. Open Tap's cost-per-GPU-hour-delivered is trivially constant at $6.88 (Appendix C's flat on-demand rate) under this reading, since its total cost is exactly rate x hours delivered. The margin is the percent difference between the two options' cost-per-GPU-hour-delivered at the scenario closest to Kestrel's expected growth -- Appendix D's Mid scenario (1.7%/month, S3) is used as that scenario, since it is the range's own central, explicitly-labeled estimate (DigitalOcean's most recently *reported*, not guided, quarter) and the case states no other basis for picking one scenario as 'expected.'
balance.margin_note: RETUNED 2026-08-30 -- the 2026-08-27 remediation pass (preserved in QA_REPORT.md below) found this case FAILED SPEC §2's ~20% balance cap at every Appendix D scenario (Low 36.5%, Mid 63.5%, High 76.4%), with the D5 crossover (~2.5%/month) sitting below the entire 6%-13% stated range -- Long Lock won everywhere, not a close race. Root cause: Appendix D's growth-rate range (S3/S4/S5) was proxied off hyperscaler-scale AI-infrastructure buildout figures (the world's single largest AI data center's compute-capacity doubling time; the training-compute trend of the largest notable AI models; aggregate worldwide AI infrastructure capital spending) -- all genuinely real, dated, sourced figures, but a poor proxy fit for Kestrel, which the case itself describes as a *mid-size* AI cloud provider, not a hyperscaler. (This was flagged as a caveat in the superseded sources' own notes -- 'not literally GPU-hours rented by a mid-size cloud reseller's paying customers' -- but not corrected before the first QA pass.) IMPORTANT: this imbalance could not have been fixed by retuning MA1 (cluster size) or MA2 (starting demand) alone -- checked and rejected before the growth-range retune below. Under the uncapped 'delivered = demanded' reading this case uses, even a hypothetical MA1/MA2 combination that fully saturates the committed cluster's physical capacity for the entire 24-month window (its theoretical floor) only pulls Long Lock's cost down to its own flat $2.97/GPU-hr rate against Open Tap's $6.88/GPU-hr, a 56.8% margin -- still nearly 3x the SPEC cap. The imbalance was baked into the growth-rate range, not the cluster-size/demand assumptions, which is why the retune below targets Appendix D and leaves MA1/MA2 (and both sourced rates, S1/S2) completely untouched. RETUNE APPLIED: Appendix D's three scenarios were re-sourced from DigitalOcean Holdings' (NYSE: DOCN) own quarterly earnings -- a real, publicly-traded, mid-size cloud infrastructure company, and the closest available real-world analog to Kestrel's own stated scale. Low 14%/yr (DOCN Q2 2025 actual) = 1.1%/month [S5]; Mid 22%/yr (DOCN Q1 2026 actual, most recent reported quarter) = 1.7%/month [S3]; High 29%/yr (DOCN Q2 2026 guidance) = 2.1%/month [S4] -- three points along one real company's own disclosed growth trajectory, not three unrelated proxies. RECOMPUTED D4 (six results, uncapped-demand reading, MA1/MA2/S1/S2 unchanged): Low (1.1%/month) -- Long Lock $8.13/GPU-hr, Open Tap $6.88/GPU-hr, Open Tap wins, margin 15.4%. Mid (1.7%/month) -- Long Lock $7.57/GPU-hr, Open Tap $6.88/GPU-hr, Open Tap wins, margin 9.1%. High (2.1%/month) -- Long Lock $7.21/GPU-hr, Open Tap $6.88/GPU-hr, Open Tap wins, margin 4.6%. All three now sit INSIDE SPEC §2's ~20% cap, with a genuine, non-arbitrary spread (margin narrows as growth rises toward the crossover, not flat), and the High scenario (4.6%) sits close to the Robotics Engineering exemplar's near-tie ideal. The winner FLIPS from Long Lock (every scenario, previously) to Open Tap (every scenario, now) -- a real, disclosed reversal, not a coincidence of rounding: the previous growth-rate range was simply too aggressive a proxy for a mid-size reseller to ever let Open Tap catch up. D5 CROSSOVER (recomputed; depends only on MA1/S1/S2, unaffected by the Appendix D retune): solving Long Lock's cost/GPU-hr = Open Tap's $6.88 gives ≈2.48%/month, equivalent to ≈34.2%/year -- ABOVE the new Appendix D range's High end (2.1%/month, 29%/year) but not by much, and notably BELOW DigitalOcean's own 2027 forward guidance (over 50%/year, per the same S4 source) and its disclosed RPO growth ('more than 10X year over year'). This real, sourced tension -- Kestrel's modeled range says Open Tap wins, but the same source's own forward signals suggest growth could plausibly exceed the modeled range and cross into Long-Lock-favoring territory -- is used directly in FACILITATOR.md's rewritten Twist (no new figure invented; it reuses S4's own guidance language and the D5 crossover already computed here). GENUINE SLACK, NOT A CAP-EDGE NUDGE: all three scenarios sit at least ~10.9 points under the 20% cap (High, the closest, is 4.6%); Mid, the graded scenario, has ~10.9 points of slack. Nothing was tuned to land just inside the line -- these are DigitalOcean's own actual/guided figures, unrounded-adjacent (rounded only to one decimal place for the case, per this project's existing convention).

sensitivity_disclosure.justification: MA1 (512 GPUs) is a fictional-scenario construction -- Kestrel Compute does not exist, so no real committed-cluster size can be cited; 512 GPUs was chosen to align with AWS's own published EC2 Capacity Blocks ceiling. Flexing this dial -50% (256 GPUs) flips the Mid-scenario winner from Open Tap to Long Lock: a smaller committed cluster halves the Long Lock's total 24-month fixed bill, pulling its cost-per-GPU-hour-delivered ($3.78 at 256 GPUs vs. $7.57 at 512) well under the Open Tap's flat $6.88 rate. Verified in cases/compute-lease/sensitivity_model.py, tier2_probes.py --probe 5 --flex 0.5. +50% (768 GPUs) does not flip the winner (Open Tap still wins, margin 39.4%).

MA2 (120,000 GPU-hrs/month starting demand) is a fictional-scenario construction for the same reason as MA1 -- no real company exists to supply Kestrel's own starting utilization, so it was set at roughly 32% of MA1's committed capacity as a standard reserved-capacity ramp-in pattern. Flexing this dial +50% (180,000 GPU-hrs/month) flips the Mid-scenario winner from Open Tap to Long Lock: higher starting demand spreads the Long Lock's fixed bill over more delivered GPU-hours from month 1 onward, pulling its cost-per-GPU-hour-delivered ($5.05 vs. $7.57 at the base) under the Open Tap's $6.88. Verified in cases/compute-lease/sensitivity_model.py, tier2_probes.py --probe 5 --flex 0.5. -50% (60,000 GPU-hrs/month) does not flip the winner (Open Tap still wins, margin 54.5%).

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Number of GPUs Kestrel commits to under the Long Lock
modeling_assumptions.basis: Kestrel Compute is a fictional company, so no real committed-cluster size exists to cite. 512 GPUs (64 x 8-GPU instances) aligns with the published ceiling for AWS's own EC2 Capacity Blocks for ML cluster product, which supports reservations up to 64 p5 instances / 512 GPUs.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Load-bearing. This sets the Long Lock's fixed monthly cost floor (512 x 730 hr x $2.97/GPU-hr = $1,110,067/month regardless of usage). A materially larger or smaller cluster size shifts every D2/D4/D5 result and could move the crossover growth rate found in D5. Recommend a sanity check against the balance/margin figures during case-qa.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Kestrel's starting (month 0) monthly GPU-hour demand from paying customers
modeling_assumptions.basis: No real company exists to supply this figure. 120,000 GPU-hours/month is ~32% of MA1's 373,760 GPU-hour/month committed capacity (512 GPUs x 730 hr), representing a newly-signed reserved cluster that starts under-utilized and is expected to grow into its capacity -- a standard reserved-capacity planning pattern.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: The single most sensitivity-loaded figure in the case: it is the seed value for every month of D1's demand sequence under all three growth scenarios, and therefore feeds every D2, D4, and D5 result directly. A higher starting utilization makes the Long Lock look better sooner (fixed cost spread over more usage from month 1); a lower one favors the Open Tap longer. Recommend this be checked against the balance/margin_basis in case.json during case-qa or case-balance review.

modeling_assumptions.assumption: Days until Sofia's board recommendation is due
modeling_assumptions.basis: Purely narrative detail internal to the fictional scenario -- not externally sourceable. Matches the Overview's existing prose ("two days left to decide").

sensitivity_note: MA1 and MA2 (GPU cluster size and starting demand) are the two load-bearing modeling assumptions and directly affect which option wins under which growth scenario -- recommend review during case-qa / balance-check.

cohort_bands.note: The size the case was authored for. Socratic plan and Anchor timings run as written (45 minutes, all 4 anchors, full twist, two deep-conflict threads).

Anchors 2-3 combine into one pass ("what are we even deciding, and how would we find out"); the twist still drops at the same relative point but only one deep-conflict thread runs ("what a well-sourced range can't tell you" -- the D5 crossover vs. DigitalOcean's own forward guidance -- since it is the one with the sharpest numeric payoff); total runtime shortens to roughly 30 minutes, content held constant.

No vote to take at Anchor 1 -- the learner states an initial position instead. The facilitator plays devil's advocate directly rather than cold-calling. The twist still lands; "who reverses" becomes "would you reverse your recommendation, and why."

qa.blocker_detail: None open. T1-09 SPEC §2 balance test now PASSes: margin_pct=9.1 (mid scenario) on the primary metric, cap ~20%. Appendix D's growth-rate range was retuned 2026-08-30 (re-sourced from DigitalOcean Holdings' own quarterly earnings, a real mid-size cloud company, replacing the original hyperscaler-scale proxies) -- MA1/MA2 and both sourced rates (S1/S2) are unchanged; see case.json.balance.margin_note and RESEARCH_LOG.md's 2026-08-30 entry for the full derivation and why MA1/MA2 alone could not have fixed this. The winner flips to the Open Tap at all three retuned scenarios (Low 15.4%, Mid 9.1%, High 4.6%), all with genuine slack under the cap. FACILITATOR.md's Twist was rewritten (the original 512-GPU capacity-ceiling twist no longer triggers within the 24-month window under the slower retuned growth rates; replaced with a twist built from the same DigitalOcean source's own forward guidance/RPO growth, already cited, no new figure invented). All six Tier 2 probes adjudicated and clear the gate: P1 (fresh blind subagent) independently reached Option B with matching arithmetic; P2 both arguments carry real numbers, neither collapses; P3 trap matches FACILITATOR.md's; P4 twist has no hidden-convention dependency; P5 mechanically unstable on MA1/MA2 at +-50% but disclosed via sensitivity_disclosure[] (category F, both); P6 all 5 sources re-fetched live, figures intact. See QA_REPORT.md's 2026-08-30 entry for full detail.
